meta.model_values_fixed: per_site.teb_dtsa and per_site.clmu_dtsa are never perturbed; only per_site.dtsa_std is.
meta.err_seeding: one independent np.random.default_rng per (scenario, record set), seed = SEED_BASE + crc32('scenario|recordset') -- byte-identical rule AND tags to review5_adderley_propagation.py, so for all19 / excl_mpls17 / core16 the realised error fields are the same fields the published observation-side block used (verified in reproduction_checks.obs_side_identity)
meta.boot_provenance: identical RNG call sequence to review5_scheme_ordering_paired.py / review5_core15.py, represented as per-record multiplicity vectors (verified in reproduction_checks.bootstrap_identity)
meta.joint_design: STOCHASTIC scenarios: error draw j paired with bootstrap resample j, j = 0..49999 (50000 joint draws); the matched unperturbed baseline on those same resamples is reported as baseline_matched_50k. DETERMINISTIC scenarios (aligned step, box fields, common-mode): all 100000 bootstrap resamples.
meta.beta_identity: beta = r*(s_m/s_o) = Cov(o,m)/Var(o) = the OLS slope of modelled on observed record means.

random_independent.spec: delta_i = E_i*K_per_Wm2, E_i ~ N(0, sigma_E^2) independent across records; sigma_E in {2,4,5,10} W/m2. Same amplitudes, tags, seeds and draw count as obs_uncertainty_v11.random_independent.

random_shared_minneapolis.spec: as random_independent but US-Minneapolis1/2 draw ONE common E (one tower, one radiometer, numerically identical offsets).

adderley_placement.spec: per-record sigma from the record's own z_rad/H by the published exponential fit sigma = exp(c0 + c1 z/H) to Adderley et al. (2015) 11.2/6.3/2.0 W/m2 at z/H = 2/3/5, run capped at 11.2 and uncapped, plus flat 11.2 and flat 9.4 W/m2. sigma values are READ from obs_uncertainty_v11.adderley_placement.per_record_sigma_Wm2.

common_mode_scale_error.spec: delta_i = s*(p/100)*<LW_up>_i*K_per_Wm2 with the record's own mean nocturnal LW_up; common_mode applies one sign to every record, random_sign draws it per record. Same amplitudes and tags as obs_uncertainty_v11.common_mode_scale_error.

aligned_step.spec: delta_i = B*sign(albedo_i - mean albedo): high-albedo records warmed by B, low-albedo records cooled by B -- the saturated sign pattern that most efficiently flattens the observed negative gradient, and therefore also the one that most efficiently COMPRESSES s_o and RAISES s_m/s_o. B = 0.25/0.5/0.75/1.0 K as in obs_uncertainty_v11.

box_obs_argmax.spec: the published worst case: the vertex of |delta_i| <= B that maximises the OBSERVED albedo--offset r (exhaustive 2^n enumeration, reproduced here and checked against obs_uncertainty_v11.unrestricted_box_worstcase), applied to the model metrics.

reproduction_checks.bootstrap_identity_verdict: The multiplicity-vector bootstrap reproduces every published one-sided probability and every published beta interval endpoint for all four record sets to < 1e-12, so the machinery used below is the published machinery.

obs_side_identity.verdict: Every observation-side statistic recomputed here from the error fields used below agrees with the published obs_uncertainty_v11 value to < 1e-15, so the perturbation fields carried into the model metrics are the SAME realised fields the published observation-side block used, not a fresh draw of the same nominal scenario.

asymmetry_diagnostics.mechanism: beta = r_{m,o} (s_m/s_o). An albedo-aligned bias that flattens the observed gradient compresses the observed spread s_o, which raises s_m/s_o at fixed s_m. Whether beta rises depends on whether the induced loss of ordering skill r_{m,o} outruns the amplitude gain.

adversarial_bounds_aimed_at_beta.spec: Not one of the published scenarios. These are the EXACT suprema over the same box |delta_i| <= B of the MODEL metrics themselves, i.e. what an unrestricted per-record radiometric bias could do if it were aimed at beta rather than at the observed correlation. sup beta and sup r are computed by bisection on the level t using the identity sup f >= t  <=>  max_box (L - t Q) >= 0 with L linear and Q convex (||z_c||^2 for beta, ||z_c|| for r), so the inner problem is a concave maximisation over a box and is solved to global optimality; max s_m/s_o is the convex minimisation of Var(o+delta).

slope_claim.statement_tested: beta = r(s_m/s_o) stays far below 1, i.e. neither scheme reproduces the observed cross-site relation
slope_claim.verdict: ROBUST to every defined observation-error scenario. Under every deterministic field (aligned step, box argmax, common-mode) the largest beta anywhere is 0.425 (box_obs_argmax/core15/B_0.75K/TEB); the single most extreme of the 50 000 random-error draws in any cell reaches 0.739 (core15/sigma_5Wm2/CLMU5) and NO random draw in any cell reaches 1; the largest tail probability P(beta>=1) is 0.0564. All are far from the 1:1 value of 1.

amplitude_claim.statement_tested: both schemes COMPRESS the cross-site amplitude, s_m/s_o < 1
amplitude_claim.verdict: CONDITIONAL on the published observed means in the conservative core. An albedo-aligned bias flattens the observed gradient, which compresses s_o and therefore RAISES s_m/s_o; in core16 and core15 the ratio crosses 1 within the amplitude range already considered, while in all19 and excl_mpls17 it does not (their s_o is ~1.8-2.0 K against ~1.04-1.07 K in the core, so the same +-B field removes a much smaller fraction of the observed spread).

claim_robustness.why_the_two_verdicts_differ: The aligned field buys amplitude at the cost of ordering. It compresses s_o, which raises s_m/s_o, but it does so by reordering the records against the model, which lowers r_{m,o} at a comparable rate. beta = r(s_m/s_o) is the product, so the two effects very nearly cancel and beta stays in a narrow band; the ratio alone does not.

manuscript_text.scope_paragraph_for_sect_model: \emph{Scope of the model conclusion}. The comparison above is conditional on the published observed record means, and we tested how conditional. Applying the observation-error scenarios of Sect.~\ref{sec:obs} to the model metrics themselves --- the observations perturbed, the two schemes' record means held fixed --- separates a robust conclusion from a conditional one. The slope conclusion is robust: independent random LW$_{\uparrow}$ error at $\sigma_E=2$--$10$~W\,m$^{-2}$ leaves $\hat\beta_{m|o}$ at a median of 0.03--0.23 with not one draw in 50\,000 reaching unity in any record set or scheme, and the albedo-aligned $\pm B$ field --- the one construction that defeats the observed association --- moves $\hat\beta_{m|o}$ only within 0.06--0.30 at $B\le1$~K; across all 208 scenario/record-set/scheme cells the tail probability $P(\hat\beta_{m|o}\ge1)$ never exceeds 0.056, reached under the aligned field at $B=0.75$~K in the conservative core for CLM-Urban, against 0.0003 there without perturbation. The \emph{amplitude} conclusion is conditional. Because an aligned bias flattens the observed gradient it compresses the observed spread --- in the conservative core from $s_o=1.07$~K to 0.65~K at $B=0.75$~K --- and so mechanically raises $s_m/s_o$, which crosses unity at $B=0.5$~K for CLM-Urban and $B=0.75$~K for TEB, with $P(s_m/s_o\ge1)$ rising from 0.05 and 0.03 to 0.83 and 0.60. The two diverge because the aligned field buys amplitude with ordering: it raises $s_m/s_o$ and lowers $r_{m,o}$ at nearly the same rate, and $\hat\beta_{m|o}$ is their product. We therefore state the model result as a slope result. That neither scheme reproduces the observed cross-site relation is robust to every observation-error scenario considered; that both schemes \emph{compress} the cross-site amplitude holds for the published means, and at every amplitude tested on all 19 and on the Minneapolis-excluded records, but in the conservative core it is conditional on the absence of an albedo-aligned radiometric bias of $0.5$~K or more. What cannot be excluded at all is narrower still: an unrestricted per-record bias field, not required to align with albedo, can reach $\hat\beta_{m|o}=1$ in the conservative core at an amplitude of $0.86$--$0.93$~K, comparable to the $0.97$~K that removes the observed association --- but it does so by annihilating the observed cross-site spread rather than by favouring either scheme, so it bounds what these records can establish about any model rather than what these two schemes do.
manuscript_text.conclusions_current_quoted:
Across 19 urban flux-tower records, the nocturnal surface--air radiometric
offset forms an organized, albedo-indexed cross-site gradient---from
radiatively decoupled, colder-than-air surfaces over open vegetated sites
to warmer-than-air dense fabric---that survives the measurement-side
robustness tests applied here (emissivity, gap-filling, the six-month
burn-in choice, sensor height, city weighting, leave-one-city-out, and
realistic radiometric measurement error).
manuscript_text.conclusions_proposed: Across 19 urban flux-tower records, the nocturnal surface--air radiometric offset forms an organized, albedo-indexed cross-site gradient---from radiatively decoupled, colder-than-air surfaces over open vegetated sites to warmer-than-air dense fabric---that survives the measurement-side robustness tests applied here (emissivity, gap-filling, the six-month burn-in choice, sensor height, city weighting, leave-one-city-out, and \emph{independent random} radiometric error at one-standard-deviation amplitudes up to 5~W\,m$^{-2}$, i.e.\ 1.0~K). Systematic error of that same size is a different matter, and we do not claim it is excluded: a bias \emph{aligned} with site albedo, of amplitude $\pm0.97$~K (peak-to-peak 1.95~K, 9.7~W\,m$^{-2}$, the size of the facet-composition discrepancy documented for hemispheric urban radiometry), would remove the conservative-core association altogether, and the collection's station metadata cannot rule one out.
manuscript_text.conclusions_model_sentence_current_quote:
whereas it does resolve the failure they
share ($P(\hat\beta_{m|o}\ge1)\le0.002$ throughout).
manuscript_text.conclusions_model_sentence_proposed: whereas it does resolve the failure they share ($P(\hat\beta_{m|o}\ge1)\le0.002$ in the three record sets, and $\le0.06$ under every observation-error scenario of Sect.~\ref{sec:obs}, the albedo-aligned one included). The amplitude statement is the weaker half of that result: an albedo-aligned bias compresses $s_o$, so $s_m/s_o$ itself rises above unity in the conservative core once the aligned amplitude reaches 0.5--0.75~K, whereas the slope does not, because the same field degrades $r_{m,o}$ at a matching rate.
manuscript_text.abstract_consistency_note: The proposed Conclusions wording matches abstract ll. 45-47 ('would be removed by an albedo-aligned radiometric bias of $\pm1$~K that the station metadata cannot exclude'), Sect. 4.1 l. 541 ('It survives the random component of plausible radiometric error but not every conceivable systematic one') and the limitation at ll. 1182-1188. The single word doing the work is the random/aligned distinction, which the current Conclusions parenthesis collapses.
manuscript_text.flag_for_lead: '$\le0.002$ throughout' in the abstract (l. 51) and Conclusions (l. 1238) is exact for all19/excl_mpls17/core16 (max 0.00131) but not for core15, whose TEB value is 0.00382 and is quoted as 0.004 at l. 677.
